{{Redirect|MMS pair|the pairing used in medicinal chemistry|Matched molecular pair analysis}}
In [[recreational mathematics]], '''Maris–McGwire–Sosa pairs''' ('''MMS pairs''', also '''MMS numbers''')<ref name="cad">{{cite web|url=http://www.cadaeic.net/maris.htm|title=Maris-McGwire-Sosa Numbers|first=Mike|last=Keith|authorlink=Mike Keith (mathematician) | year=1998|website=cadeic.net|accessdate=6 June 2017}}</ref> {{OEIS|id=A045759}} are two consecutive [[natural number]]s such that adding each number's digits (in [[base 10]]) to the digits of its [[prime factorization]] gives the same sum.

:Thus  61 → 6 + 1 (the sum of its digits) + 6 + 1 (since 61 is its prime factorization)
:and   62 → 6 + 2 (the sum of its digits) + 3 + 1 + 2 (since 31 × 2 is its prime factorization).

The above two sums are equal (= 14), so 61 and 62 form an MMS pair.

MMS pairs are so named because in [[1998 Major League Baseball home run record chase|1998]] the [[baseball]] players [[Mark McGwire]] and [[Sammy Sosa]] both hit their 62nd [[home run]]s for the season, passing the old record of 61, held by [[Roger Maris]]. American engineer [[Mike Keith (mathematician)|Mike Keith]] noticed this property of these numbers and named pairs of numbers like these MMS pairs.<ref>{{cite book
|chapter-url=https://archive.org/details/adamspencersbook0000spen/page/101/mode/1up |chapter-url-access=registration |chapter=62
|title=Adam Spencer's Book of Numbers
|first=Adam |last=Spencer
|year=2004
|publisher=Thunder's Mouth Press
|page=101
|isbn=1-56858-289-7
}}</ref>
